findings.title: Optimized Python removes the validator consistency and hash checks
findings.reproduction: Run the documented validator with PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 inherited in the environment, or with python3 -O, while a schema-valid report has a wrong Linux artifact hash or mismatched source/check metadata.
findings.expected: Refuse invalid evidence or explicitly refuse optimized execution before writing a passed validation receipt.
findings.observed: 28 assert statements implement the consistency, hash, count, source and staged-evidence checks. There is no __debug__ guard. CPython 3.14.4 compilation without executing the code object shows 505 top-level instructions at the checked assertion lines with optimize=0 and zero with optimize=1; references() loses its sha lookup. JSON schema validation and duplicate-key refusal survive, so this is not a claim that every check disappears.
findings.impact: A schema-valid inconsistent report can produce validation=passed under an ordinary Python runtime option. This affects the audit evidence checker, not MnemoCode runtime/recovery or the independently reconciled current 2988 project results.
findings.recommendedFix: Before validation, explicitly refuse optimization with an if not __debug__: raise RuntimeError(...) guard, or replace evidence-critical asserts with explicit checked raises that survive optimization.
findings.requiredVerification: Main should confirm optimized execution refuses before replacing report-validation.json, and the ordinary documented invocation still accepts the exact correct evidence. Reviewer did not execute either invocation.

findings.title: Hash-valid receipts can be paired with contradictory reported execution identities
findings.reproduction: Keep every bound receipt/log unchanged but replace executions[0].sourceBefore and sourceAfter with the same different 64-character fingerprint. This changes only the public report metadata and leaves all current validator predicates and local-reference hashes satisfied.
findings.expected: Reported execution facts must equal the facts in the hash-bound receipt. Source fingerprints written in the validation receipt must be derived from the retained ordered path/hash rows.
findings.observed: references() checks receipt file hashes but never compares their JSON contents with the surrounding execution entry. The execution loop requires only exitCode=0, stopReason=null and sourceBefore=sourceAfter. The supplied canonical schema does not constrain executions. In addition, the runtime/documentation sourceFingerprint values are compared or copied as strings, never recomputed from source rows; a changed docs.sourceFingerprint with its legitimate reference-hash refresh would also be reported without verification.
findings.impact: The new normal-mode consistency checker can accept contradictory source/receipt metadata. All 13 actual current execution records do match their receipts, and both actual source fingerprints recomputed correctly in this review; this is a validator false-acceptance defect, not a finding of falsified current results.
findings.recommendedFix: Read each already hash-verified execution receipt and compare sourceBefore/sourceAfter, exitCode, stopReason and corresponding log identity with the report fields. Recompute the runtime and documentation fingerprints using the retained ordered-row JSON serialization and compare their stored values. Command comparison must preserve the intentional public home-path anonymization.
findings.requiredVerification: Main should check a controlled wrong execution fingerprint and wrong documentation fingerprint are refused while the exact current records remain accepted. No report, receipt or source was modified and no validator invocation was executed by this reviewer.

findings.title: The new validator depends on unpinned third-party Python input
findings.reproduction: Reproduce the new validator in an environment without the original preinstalled jsonschema distribution, or with a different distribution version.
findings.expected: The new harness declares reproducible third-party Python inputs according to TOOL-03, or names an explicit approved pin source.
findings.observed: The harness imports jsonschema. Its directory contains only run.mjs, README.md and validate.py; no adjacent hash-pinned requirement manifest exists. The README names the existing AUD-035 installation but provides no exact version or hash-pinned installation input for this new harness.
findings.impact: Reproduction depends on unspecified host packages and can fail at import or use a different validator stack. No package was installed during review, no upstream vulnerability is alleged, and no wider audit of historical harnesses was performed.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare the already used validator and required transitive Python dependencies in an adjacent hash-pinned requirements file and document pip install --require-hashes with that file; alternatively identify the exact owner-approved shared pin source and make its use reproducible. No new MnemoCode runtime dependency is needed.
findings.requiredVerification: Main should retain the existing validator version/hash provenance and the documented dependency recipe. A network installation or clean-environment replay was not performed by this reviewer.
